note: One box, four different jobs: the shape at a slow tempo, its roots alone, the shape faster over drums, then a short improvisation that ends on the root. The root stays lit in every view.

exercise.title: A minor pentatonic, box 1
exercise.focus: A minor pentatonic · box 1 · 60 then 80 bpm
exercise.why: Box 1 is the home base most lead playing starts from; knowing where its roots are lets you end a phrase anywhere.

sections.text: Box 1 is the first scale shape most guitarists learn because every note sits under four fingers at the 5th fret.
Play box 1 from the low {{1}} up to the high E string and back down, one note per click, alternate picking. Index finger on the 5th fret, ring or pinky on the 7th and 8th.
Now play only the {{1}} notes in the box: the A on the low E, the A on the D string, the A on the high E. Low to high and back, saying "A" as you play each one.
The whole box again, now at 80 with drums. Start each run on a different {{1}}: the low one, then the one on the D string. Done when two runs in a row have no missed notes.

Keep the drums going and play short phrases of three or four notes from the box, leaving a gap after each. End every phrase on a {{1}}. This scale is the one used in blues and rock, so it will sound right whatever you choose.
